findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification
findings.body: Password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The backup-code branch (line 131) does not verify password at all. An attacker who knows only a victim's email and one valid backup code can send both `totpCode=<anything>` and `backupCode=<valid>` to /api/auth/callback/credentials: the dummy totpCode skips the password check, the backup branch ignores totp validity and grants login. This turns a second factor into a password replacement and allows account takeover without the password.

findings.title: Backup-code single-use is not atomic and allows concurrent reuse
findings.body: Login does read-decrypt-indexOf, then sets `backupCodes[index]=null` and writes back with a separate prisma update. Two concurrent authorize calls with the same backup code can both read the same array, both find the index, and both succeed before either write nulls it. This violates the advertised exactly-once property and lets one code be used twice.

findings.title: Existing 2FA users can never obtain backup codes
findings.body: Setup rejects with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled if twoFactorEnabled is true. The migration adds nullable backupCodes, so all pre-existing 2FA users have NULL. There is no regenerate endpoint, so they stay without codes forever, login/disable with backup always returns MissingBackupCodes, and the UI message telling them to generate codes in settings is a dead end.

findings.title: Backup-code handling crashes on non-string input and rejects pasted codes
findings.body: Disable calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll without type check, trim, or case normalization. A non-string value (array/object/number) throws TypeError and returns 500 instead of 400. Pasted codes with trailing spaces/newlines from the downloaded file also fail because only dashes are stripped. The same pattern exists in next-auth-options authorize, so login has the same crash and usability failure.

findings.title: Exhausted backup codes reported as incorrect instead of missing
findings.body: Used codes are nulled in place, so after 10 uses the column contains JSON like [null,...] which is truthy. The check only tests column null, so exhausted users fall through to indexOf failure and get IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes. They cannot distinguish wrong vs exhausted, and with no regeneration endpoint they are permanently stuck if they lose their authenticator.

findings.title: Backup codes kept only in memory are permanently lost on refresh
findings.body: Codes are fetched at setup time and held only in React state, then shown after enable succeeds. If the user reloads, closes the tab, or loses network between enable and saving, the in-memory codes are gone. Because setup is blocked once twoFactorEnabled is true and there is no re-view or regenerate API, the user permanently loses their backup codes immediately after enrollment.
